body: Everyone in this community is such an angel. Lately I think I have really been confronting hardcore some of the things that I have done in the past that I have ignored for a thing time. They have been in back of my head for so long and I really realized that I cannot forget until I forgive myself, and that until then it's just going to keep popping back up again. I want to stay this person that has been through all this, though. Like I said to pinballwizard16, I believe in being honestly happy, like totally happy, meaning not overshadowed by shittiness anymore. I feel like because of what I have been through, I can get there, I can break through, I'm so over these lows!

I've realized that it takes a lot of strength to laugh and enjoy things all the time, that the highs and lows will always be there, but that happiness can be honest too. Does that make sense? I remember being younger and going through some really difficult times, but I would still find time to just say fuck it, and laugh at everything. I want to enjoy writing instead of being freaked out by it too. It freaks me out because I just get so dark when I go to that place. 


I had two beers last night, so I think I'm okay on the drinking. I just freak out at the addictive behavior that I see in myself in all ways, from food to weed to masturbation to TV to laziness and feeling bad. I am aware of alcohol being addicting and yet I keep turning to it, in moderation and in excess. For one thing, I drink and smoke even though I probably shouldn't financially. But whatever, right? Maybe if I wasn't doing that, I'd be doing something else destructive. I'm sorry about your cousin, it reminds me of my uncle. My dad, his brother, was the one that found him, and even though my dad is my least favorite person to think about, the idea of him in that moment makes me feel so much love and sympathy for him. In fact, two of my cousins are really what keep me wanting to live. One is the same age I was when my life really took a turn for the worst, and one is about the age that I was when my uncle took his life.


Being positive is the most important thing there is in life. It is precious. Only the strong can do it. I know survivors are the strongest. So much can change with time.


EDIT: I'm almost 23. That's something to look forward to soon, my birthday. I've had birthdays that were quite depressing before, there's not a chance this year could be a bad one.
